rounds.q: What % of the air you breathe is oxygen?
rounds.why: Nitrogen is 78%. Even argon, at 0.9%, beats carbon dioxide (0.04%) by over 20 times.
rounds.src: NOAA JetStream, The Atmosphere (dry air composition, current)
rounds.fun: Only about 1 part in 5 of the air is oxygen. Breathe deep!

rounds.q: How many elements are on the periodic table?
rounds.why: The last 4 were named in 2016, and one, tennessine, is named after Tennessee.
rounds.src: IUPAC, Names of the Elements 113, 115, 117 and 118 (2016)
rounds.fun: 118 elements, and Tennessee got one named after it. Yeehaw!

rounds.q: How many seconds does thunder take to travel one mile?
rounds.why: If you count 30 seconds or less from flash to thunder, it's time to get to shelter.
rounds.src: NOAA National Weather Service, Lightning Science (current)
rounds.fun: Count the seconds, divide by 5, and you know how many miles away it is!

rounds.q: At 5,000 feet up, water boils at what temperature in °F?
rounds.why: Every 500 feet you climb drops water's boiling point by about 1°F.
rounds.src: New Mexico State University, High-Altitude Cooking (current)
rounds.fun: From 212 down to 202. That's a 10 degree drop just by climbing!

rounds.q: When water freezes, by about what % does it grow?
rounds.why: That's why only about 10% of an ice cube or iceberg pokes above the water.
rounds.src: USGS Water Science School, Water Density (current)
rounds.fun: Ice puffs up about 9% bigger. No wonder it floats!
